intro: Lean hogs settle in cash on the CME Lean Hog Index, which the desk rebuilds daily. Unlike dairy, the index is a two-day average, so there is no monthly average to lock in; the tests below ask whether the cash index, its seasonal path or the packer margin say more than the futures do. Positions are shown only for ideas that held up in every period tested.

trades.name: Cash-index convergence (lean hogs)
trades.thesis: Lean hog futures settle on the CME Lean Hog Index, a two-day average of what packers paid. The desk rebuilds the index from USDA's daily report a day before CME posts it and estimates where it will be at expiry (cash now x a walk-forward model of seasonality, momentum and the packer margin). Best tested setting: within 13 weeks of expiry, gap above 1.0 ¢/lb. Close to zero in at least one period tested, so no reliable edge; shown for reference, not as a trade. Accuracy check in the last 2 weeks: futures miss the final index by 1.54% on average, the model by 2.12%.
trades.entry: Wednesday after the close: for each hog contract within 13 weeks of expiry, if the settlement estimate is above the futures by more than 1.0 ¢/lb, buy one lot; if below by more than that, sell one.
trades.exit: Re-check each Wednesday; close when the gap falls back inside the threshold or flips, or hold to final settlement (the index on the 10th business day of the month).
trades.risk: The index can move several dollars in two weeks around seasonal turns (spring rally, late-summer top); no stop was used in the test.

trades.name: 4-week futures trend (lean hogs)
trades.thesis: Hog prices trend through the seasonal cycle; futures partly inherit that persistence. Close to zero in at least one period tested, so no reliable edge; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Wednesday: one lot per contract up to 6 months out, in the direction of its 4-week change when that change exceeds the cost.
trades.exit: Flip or flatten when the 4-week change reverses.
trades.risk: Many positions at once; size small.
track: 4-week change and the seasonal table (this page, nightly)

trades.name: Expiry drift (lean hogs)
trades.thesis: Checks whether being long hog contracts in their last weeks has paid, as it has for live cattle. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Hold one lot long in each hog contract 4-13 weeks from expiry.
trades.risk: Unhedged long exposure to the cash index.

trades.name: Seasonal pattern (lean hogs)
trades.thesis: The same contract has moved the same way over the same 4 calendar weeks in at least 70% of the last 5-10 years. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Wednesday: one lot in the direction of the historical 4-week move, for contracts 2 weeks to 6 months out.
trades.exit: Re-check weekly; flatten when the pattern no longer qualifies.
trades.risk: Many positions at once; size small.
track: 4-week change and the seasonal table (this page, nightly)

trades.name: Breakout with trailing stop: lean hogs
trades.thesis: Wins less than half the time; stops keep losers small and the occasional long run pays for them. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Daily, on the nearest contract at least 45 days from expiry (2026-12): buy on a settle above the 20-day high (now 70.950); sell on a settle below the 20-day low (now 64.675).
trades.exit: Long: a settle below the 10-day low or the trailing stop (2x the 20-day average daily move below the best close). Short: the mirror. Flat 10 days before expiry.
trades.risk: Average daily move 0.741 ¢/lb = $297 per lot; the stop sits about twice that away.
track: Daily settlement vs the 20-day high/low and the stop (this page, nightly)
